newsitem.title: FINLAND: FOCUS - TRADING LOSSES HIT NESTE 1996 PROFIT.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - TRADING LOSSES HIT NESTE 1996 PROFIT.

text.p: Finnish oil and energy group Neste Oy on Friday reported a sharp fall in 1996 profit, due mainly to heavy losses in crude oil derivatives trading, but said it had plugged the gap and predicted improvement this year.

Profit before extraordinary items was 566 million markka ($112.4 million), down from 1.36 billion in 1995 although slightly better than the median market expectation of 410 million and well within the 200-725 million markka range of analysts' forecasts.
Analysts said the operating profit was disappointing and brokers said the proposed 2.00 markka dividend -- down from 2.40 for 1995 -- was also viewed negatively.
Neste shares fell 4.50 markka to 140.00 by noon as investors took profits. The shares had risen 20 percent in February ahead of the results and 30 percent this year.
Group net sales were unchanged at 43 billion markka.
Neste said it now aimed to slim its crude trading operations to below 10 billion markka in net sales from 16 billion last year.
"From our point of view, it would make sense (for trading) to go below 10 billion markka in net sales," president and chief operating officer Jukka Viinanen told a news conference.
Neste said losses in crude trading amounted to 560 million markka last year, up from 495 million reported for the January-August period, but it no longer had major exposure.

"The trading contracts due to mature in 1998 that were open at the turn of the year were closed at the end of February 1997. Consequently, the group no longer has trading contracts that would have a material impact on earnings in future years," it said in a statement.
It said the increase in the losses was due to the strengthening of the dollar and the fact that commitments due at the end of this year were booked as liabilities in 1996.

Neste said its refining profitability improved, helped by stronger refining margins internationally, but increased retail competition capped the unit's overall results and the refining margin would remain unsatisfactory at $1 to $1.50 per barrel.
"At this level new (refining) investment is impossible," Viinanen said.
Falling prices also weakened its chemicals business but exploration and production doubled its profit and Neste expected this year to bring an overall improvement.
"The final tertial showed signs of recovery and considering the trading write-off, our actual business operation is on a firm footing," Viinanen said. "1997 will be better than 1996."
Looking further ahead, Neste said it expected growth in natural gas, which was likely to be the main growing sector.

"Neste will become more of a gas company," chairman Jaakko Ihamuotila said but gave no specific targets. Neste said it expected natural gas consumption in Finland to grow eight percent this year from 3.5 billion cubic metres in 1996.
Neste is the country's only importer of natural gas.
It added that as it closed its accounts, it was still in talks on the sale of its 50 percent stake in petrochemicals venture Borealis, jointly owned with Norway's Statoil.
($ = 5.033 Finnish Markka)
